domain_restrictions: When r = 0, the empty product is interpreted as 1.
The expression is intended in a setting where the product formula is meaningful, either formally or after excluding denominator zeros if evaluated numerically.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every pair of integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is symmetric under replacing r by n-r: [n choose r]_q equals [n choose n-r]_q.
quantifier_order: For all integers n and r, assume 0 <= r <= n.
With q treated as a fixed formal parameter or variable, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by the given product formula.
Then the equality [n choose r]_q equals [n choose n-r]_q holds.

variables.name: r
variables.role: index parameter constrained by 0 <= r <= n

variables.name: q
variables.role: base parameter of the q-binomial coefficient

witness_dependencies: The value of [n choose r]_q depends on n, r, and q.
The equality compares two quantities with the same q parameter and complementary indices r and n-r.

statement_nl: For integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := product_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q.
